title: Nairobi vs Kampala: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Nairobi is your pick for a dynamic, modern African city experience with unparalleled wildlife access and a more developed infrastructure, budgeting around $70-150 USD daily for a comfortable mid-range trip. categories.name: h2 id="costs-budget">💰 Costs & Budget
categories.summary: Kampala offers a significantly lower cost of living and travel, making it far more accessible for budget travelers.

categories.name: h2 id="getting-there-around">✈️ Getting There & Around
categories.summary: Nairobi offers better international flight connectivity and a more diverse, generally safer range of transport options within the city.

categories.name: h2 id="accommodation">🏨 Accommodation
categories.summary: Nairobi offers a broader selection of accommodation options, from high-end luxury to modern mid-range, with generally higher standards of service and amenities.

categories.name: h2 id="food-scene">🍽️ Food Scene
categories.summary: Nairobi boasts a more diverse and sophisticated culinary landscape, with a wider array of international cuisines and fine dining experiences.

categories.name: h2 id="nightlife-entertainment">🕺 Nightlife & Entertainment
categories.summary: Kampala's nightlife is legendary for its vibrant energy, affordability, and incredibly friendly, welcoming atmosphere.

categories.name: h2 id="culture-attractions">🏛️ Culture & Attractions
categories.summary: Both cities provide distinct and rich cultural experiences, with Nairobi blending wildlife and modern history, and Kampala focusing on traditional heritage.

categories.name: h2 id="nature-day-trips">🌳 Nature & Day Trips
categories.summary: Nairobi offers unparalleled, immediate access to diverse and iconic wildlife experiences, including a national park within the city limits and serves as the main gateway to world-renowned safaris.

categories.name: h2 id="safety-security">👮 Safety & Security
categories.summary: Kampala generally offers a more relaxed atmosphere and is perceived by travelers as slightly safer, with less prevalent violent crime against tourists compared to Nairobi.

categories.name: h2 id="digital-nomad-friendliness">💻 Digital Nomad Friendliness
categories.summary: Nairobi provides superior infrastructure with reliable high-speed internet, numerous co-working spaces, and a thriving tech ecosystem, making it more conducive for remote work.

categories.name: h2 id="overall-vibe-people">😊 Overall Vibe & People
categories.summary: Kampala consistently wins hearts with its famously friendly locals, welcoming atmosphere, and vibrant, community-oriented spirit.

faq.question: What's the best time to visit Nairobi or Kampala?
faq.answer: Both cities generally experience two dry seasons: January-February and June-October. These periods offer the most pleasant weather for exploring and are ideal for wildlife viewing in nearby parks. Avoid the heavy rains of March-May and November-December, which can make travel challenging.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kenya and Uganda?
faq.answer: Most nationalities require an eVisa for Kenya (apply online before arrival). For Uganda, many nationalities also require an eVisa. The East Africa Tourist Visa (EATV) covers Kenya, Uganda, and Rwanda with a single application, costing $100 and valid for 90 days, if you plan to visit multiple countries.

faq.question: Is malaria a concern in both cities?
faq.answer: Yes, both Nairobi and Kampala are in malaria-risk areas. It's highly recommended to consult your doctor about antimalarial medication. Additionally, use insect repellent, sleep under mosquito nets, and wear long sleeves and trousers, especially during dawn and dusk.

faq.question: How long should I spend in each city?
faq.answer: For Nairobi, a minimum of 3-4 days is ideal to cover city attractions and a day trip to Nairobi National Park. If planning a safari, add 3-5 extra days. For Kampala, 2-3 days allows you to experience the main cultural sites and nightlife. If using it as a base for gorilla trekking, add 4-5 days for travel and the trek itself.

faq.question: Can I travel between Nairobi and Kampala easily?
faq.answer: Yes, direct flights between Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO) and Entebbe International Airport (EBB) take approximately 1 hour and are operated by Kenya Airways and Uganda Airlines, costing around $150-250 USD. Overland travel by bus is also an option, taking 12-16 hours and costing around $25-40 USD.

faq.question: What unique experiences does each city offer that the other doesn't?
faq.answer: Nairobi uniquely offers the 'safari in the city' experience with Nairobi National Park, plus direct access to world-renowned safaris like Maasai Mara. Kampala's unique draw is its incredibly vibrant, authentic nightlife and its status as a direct gateway to the famous gorilla trekking experiences in western Uganda.

faq.question: Are both cities good for solo female travelers?
faq.answer: Both cities require a high degree of caution for solo female travelers. Nairobi has a reputation for higher petty crime rates and harassment, especially at night. Kampala is often perceived as friendlier but still requires vigilance, particularly with bodabodas and avoiding walking alone after dark. Always share your itinerary and use trusted transport.

faq.question: What's the internet situation for staying connected?
faq.answer: Nairobi has more reliable and faster internet infrastructure, with numerous co-working spaces and cafes offering strong Wi-Fi. Kampala's internet can be less consistent, though many cafes offer Wi-Fi, and buying a local SIM card (e.g., MTN, Airtel) with data bundles is cheap and effective in both cities for staying connected.
